headline: Turkish Central Bank Exempts Certain Corporate Loans from Credit Limits
summary: The Central Bank of Turkey issued a directive exempting Turkish lira-denominated loans extended for the repayment of domestic private sector debt securities from credit growth limits.
why: Central bank credit regulations directly influence corporate liquidity and refinancing capacity for maturing bond debt. This targeted exemption aims to ease refinancing pressures for non-bank private entities.

impacts.name: Banking
impacts.why: Exempting specific corporate repayment loans from credit caps alters risk allocation and lending volumes for commercial banks.

why_moved: Easing credit limits for specific corporate debt repayments reduces default risks and enhances liquidity access for private issuers, supporting domestic debt markets.
